result.title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
result.comment: Agent Evaluation Science Symposium, Fall 2026, New York City
result.summary: Coding agents now write whole codebases in long autonomous runs, guided mainly by whether their tests pass. Yet passing tests alone does not reveal accumulating complexity or gaps in test coverage, which then persist as agents extend their own code. We introduce metrics-in-the-loop, an inference-time intervention that gives agents in-flight feedback: cheap, automatically computed code metrics injected into the agent's context during the trajectory. After each code-changing agent turn, we insert short feedback messages naming changed functions whose cyclomatic complexity exceeds a limit (complexity feedback) or changed lines that are skipped by tests (coverage feedback), giving the agent the opportunity to refactor code or strengthen tests before continuing. We run extensive experiments and ablations comparing several interventions across three long-horizon coding benchmarks and four strong models. We find that complexity feedback significantly reduces erosion, a measure of complexity concentration of code, without affecting held-out correctness of the code. Broadly, our experiments investigate a practical form of agent "re-railing", where timely, actionable measurements redirect agents before weaknesses become the foundation they keep building on. As agents scale to codebases with millions of lines, such interventions become critical to sustaining effective development and long-term code maintainability.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出「metrics-in-the-loop」：在编码 agent 的长程轨迹中，每轮修改代码后注入廉价自动计算的反馈（圈复杂度超限、测试未覆盖的改动行），让 agent 有机会即时重构或补测，并在三个长程编码基准、四个模型上做实验与消融。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是「用低成本自动度量在轨迹中途纠偏」，与 LVR 中如何依据内部状态指标决定继续、回看证据或停止的机制可能相通，可供核查；但对象是代码复杂度与测试覆盖，与视觉推理表征无直接联系。
